tasks.request: Please add a method `Inventory.write_off(sku, qty, at)` to `stockroom/inventory.py` for stock that is damaged, lost or expired. It removes `qty` units of `sku` from on-hand stock, records a `Movement` with reason `"write_off"` and a negative delta of `-qty` at time `at`, and returns the new on-hand level. It must not be possible to write off more units than are on hand or to write off a nonsensical quantity. Please add a test for it.

assertions.why: requested behaviour on an input no convention decides
rule 14: non-issue removal emits exactly one WARNING '<reason> <qty> x <SKU>' via a stockroom.* logger -> 'write_off 3 x BLT-0001'
rule 4: taking more than on hand raises InsufficientStockError 'insufficient stock for NUT-0001: requested 5, on hand 3'
rule 3: qty 0 raises InvalidQuantityError 'quantity must be a positive integer, got 0'

tasks.request: Pickers often pull several items for one order, so please add a method `Inventory.issue_many(lines, at)` to `stockroom/inventory.py`. `lines` is a sequence of `(sku, qty)` pairs; each line is issued exactly like `Inventory.issue` (an `"issue"` movement with delta `-qty` at time `at`, recorded in the order of the lines). The method returns a generated identifier for the batch; batch identifiers use the prefix `BAT`. Please add a test.

assertions.why: requested behaviour on an input no convention decides
rule 12: a failing line raises its error and leaves on-hand levels and history exactly as before
rule 12: the first failing line in input order (unknown SKU) determines the raised error
rule 13: '<PREFIX>-<n>' zero-padded to 6 digits, per-Inventory counter from 1 -> BAT-000001, BAT-000002, new inventory BAT-000001

tasks.request: Please add a method `Inventory.record_count(counts, at)` to `stockroom/inventory.py` for applying the result of a physical stock count. `counts` is a mapping of SKU to the counted number of units (a non-negative int). For every SKU in the mapping whose counted quantity differs from the current on-hand level, set the on-hand level to the counted quantity and record a `Movement` with reason `"count_adjust"` and delta `counted - previous_on_hand` at time `at`; SKUs whose count matches get no movement. The method returns a generated identifier for the count; count identifiers use the prefix `CNT`. Please add a test.

assertions.why: requested behaviour on an input no convention decides
rule 14: negative adjustment emits exactly one WARNING '<reason> <qty> x <SKU>' via stockroom.* logger -> 'count_adjust 4 x BLT-0001'
rule 12: a stock count with a failing line (unknown SKU) raises and changes nothing
rule 13: per-Inventory counter, 6-digit padding -> CNT-000001, CNT-000002, fresh inventory CNT-000001

tasks.request: Please add a function `average_unit_cost_cents(inventory)` to `stockroom/valuation.py` that returns the weighted average unit cost of the stock currently on hand: the total stock value divided by the total number of units on hand across all items.

assertions.why: requested behaviour on an input no convention decides
rule 6: ROUND_HALF_EVEN to whole cents: 250/100 -> 2, 350/100 -> 4
rule 8: average over zero units returns None

tasks.request: Please add a function `value_share_percent(inventory, sku)` to `stockroom/valuation.py` that returns the given item's share of the total stock value (on hand x unit cost, across all items) as a percentage, e.g. an item holding a quarter of the stock value gives 25.

assertions.why: requested behaviour on an input no convention decides
rule 9: Decimal, 0-100, one decimal place, ROUND_HALF_UP: 1/16 -> Decimal('6.3'); 1/1 -> Decimal('100.0')

tasks.request: Please add a method `Inventory.movements_between(start, end, sku=None)` to `stockroom/inventory.py` that returns the recorded movements whose timestamp falls within the period from `start` to `end` (both datetimes), optionally restricted to one SKU like `Inventory.history`. Please add a test.

assertions.why: requested behaviour on an input no convention decides
rule 10: start <= at < end: movement at start included, at end excluded
rule 10: start >= end raises InvalidPeriodError (stockroom.errors, StockroomError+ValueError) 'period start must be before end'
rule 5: tuple, movements in recorded order (not timestamp order)

assertions.why: requested behaviour on an input no convention decides
